newsitem.title: USA: GM to sell four parts plants - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM to sell four parts plants - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp intends to sell four of its parts plants in the United States and Canada to a new company created by an investment firm, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday.
The newspaper cited "people close to the matter" as saying the automobile maker would sell the plants that belong to its Delphi Automotive Systems unit to Peregrine Inc.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed, it said.
The newspaper said Peregrine, which was formed by Joseph Littlejohn & Levy, had signed a memo of understanding with General Motors to close the deal by the end of the year.
The plants, which make parts for a vehicle's interior like door parts, generate about $1 billion a year in sales, it said.
Although Peregrine will be independent of General Motors, it will probably be assured of several billion dollars of business "the next few years" from the company, it added.
